body.statement: As \(u\to\infty\), \(\Pr\{D(0)>u,R_{\mathrm c}(0)>R(u)\}=o\{\Delta(u)\lambda(u)\}\), \(\lambda(u)>0\), and \(\mathfrak L(u)\ne\varnothing\) eventually. There are unique universal constants \(\beta_{\star}>0\), \(\gamma_{\star}\in\mathbb R\), and \(c_{\star}\in\mathbb R\) such that \(\mathcal E_{\star}(u)=\beta_{\star}u+\gamma_{\star}\log u+c_{\star}\in\mathfrak E\), \(-\log\lambda(u)=\mathcal E_{\star}(u)+o(1)\), and \(\lambda(u+x)/\lambda(u)\to e^{-\beta_{\star}x}\) uniformly for \(x\) in each compact subset of \(\mathbb R\). In the exact uniform regime \(\ell(u)\in\mathfrak L(u)=[u^3,\lambda(u)^{-1/2}]\), \(\sup_{\ell\in\mathfrak L(u)}|\Pr\{\sup_{0\le t\le\ell}D(t)>u\}/\{\ell\lambda(u)\}-1|\to0\). The expansion implies \(\mathcal E_{\star}'(u)>0\) for every \(u\ge u_0\), so the displayed definitions of \(b(T)\) and positive \(a(T)\) are valid only on \([T_0,\infty)\). As \(T\to\infty\) through this domain, and hence eventually with \(u_{\mathrm p}(T)\ge u_0\), \(\mathcal N_T\) converges to a Poisson random measure with intensity \(dt\,e^{-x}dx\), and \(\Pr\{[M_T-b(T)]/a(T)\le x\}\to\exp\{-e^{-x}\}\). The padded grid target obeys \(\{M_T^{\mathrm{sim}}-M_T\}/a(T)\to0\) in probability on the same eventual domain. These growing-domain assertions strictly strengthen the one-location Brownian--GCM LR law of Banerjee and Wellner (2001), recovered at \(D(0)\).
body.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: simultaneous LR calibration requires the rare-event law of the LR energy field, not the fixed-point law.
body.gap: Banerjee and Wellner (2001) give \(D(0)\); Hooghiemstra and Lopuhaä (1998) and Durot, Kulikov, and Lopuhaä (2012) give extremes for argmax or slope error, not for \(D\).
body.consumer: The theorem supplies reusable critical values for any regular monotone model whose local LR statistic reduces to the same Brownian--GCM energy field.

obligation.what_is_open: The sharp one-cluster high-excursion expansion, additive tail ratio, positive runs-declustered intensity, uniform rare-block law, marked Poisson limit, Gumbel maximum law, and growing-window grid approximation are not derived.
obligation.obstruction: Exact Brownian scaling identifies the small-noise speed but no supplied theorem establishes an infinite-domain contraction principle for this nonlinear GCM energy. A logarithmic large-deviation rate would still not determine the translation mode, prefactor, additive constant, anticlustering, or maximum approximation required by the claim.
obligation.attempted: The exact small-noise scaling, a projection lower bound on the variational energy, and a localized finite-energy plateau witness were proved. The prescribed PAVA window and mesh check reproduced the witness. Moderate-threshold numerical evidence was not used as a substitute for the missing asymptotic analysis.
obligation.partial_result:
Let \(\Phi(h)\) be the origin-constrained LR energy obtained from \(t^2+h(t)\), for an absolutely continuous Cameron--Martin perturbation \(h\).  If \(h_b(t)=b^2h(t/b)\), affine and spatial equivariance of the constrained and unconstrained GCMs give
\[
 \Phi(h_b)=b^3\Phi(h),
 \qquad
 \frac12\int_{\mathbb R}h_b'(t)^2\,dt
 =b^3\frac12\int_{\mathbb R}h'(t)^2\,dt.
\]
Brownian scaling with \(b=u^{1/3}\) therefore yields the exact distributional identity
\[
 \Pr\{D(0)>u\}=\Pr\{\Phi(u^{-1/2}\mathbb W)>1\}.
\]
Define the deterministic variational energy
\[
 I_\star=\inf\left\{\frac12\int_{\mathbb R}h'(t)^2\,dt:\Phi(h)\ge1\right\}.
\]
On a finite interval containing the contact set, let \(\mathcal C_0\subset\mathcal C\) be the constrained and unconstrained monotone slope cones.  Since the baseline slope \(2t\) belongs to \(\mathcal C_0\), the Hilbert-space projection identity gives
\[
 \Phi(h)
 =\operatorname{dist}^2(2t+h',\mathcal C_0)
  -\operatorname{dist}^2(2t+h',\mathcal C)
 \le \|h'\|_2^2.
\]
Thus \(I_\star\ge1/2\).  Conversely, take \(k=4^{1/3}\), \(a=k/4\), and
\[
 h'(t)=(k-2t)\mathbf 1\{-a\le t\le k/2\}.
\]
Then \(2t+h'(t)\) is nondecreasing and is constant at \(k\) on \([-a,k/2]\).  Its zero-constrained projection replaces this constant by zero on \([-a,0]\), while the unrestricted projection leaves it unchanged.  Consequently
\[
 \Phi(h)=ak^2=\frac{k^3}{4}=1,
 \qquad
 \frac12\int h'(t)^2\,dt
 =\frac{(k+2a)^3}{12}=\frac98,
\]
so
\[
 \frac12\le I_\star\le\frac98.
\]
The prescribed midpoint PAVA reconnaissance reproduced this localized plateau across windows \(R=4,8,16\): the respective \((\mathrm{LR},\mathrm{energy})\) pairs were \((0.984313,1.107396)\) on mesh \(1/64\), \((1.004000,1.129493)\) on mesh \(1/128\), and \((1.004000,1.129503)\) on mesh \(1/256\).  These deterministic and numerical checks do not establish a Brownian large-deviation principle on the infinite domain.  Even a logarithmic tail rate would not determine the additive \(o(1)\) expansion, translation-mode prefactor, runs-declustered intensity, anticlustering, or the marked Poisson limit demanded by the target.
